material.origin: Original synthetic author model; no real specimen, instrument reading, teacher experiment or independent measurement exists. Generated amounts use stoichiometric bookkeeping; pH uses ideal Henderson-Hasselbalch with pKa=4.76 at 25 C and dilute ideal activities. Strong-acid/base blank uses stoichiometric excess and pKw=14.00. Small dissociation corrections, activity changes and indicator consumption are omitted. The column called species amount is a model output, not pH-independent analytical evidence.
material.noAcetateControlStart: Initially 100 mL water adjusted with a trace of HCl to pH 4.760; the same stated acid/base amounts and volumes are then added. These too are modeled values, not measured controls.
material.dilutionOnlyControlStart: A separate identical initial acetate/acetic acid sample receives only water to the same successive volumes. These too are modeled values, not measured controls.

materialDe:
Modellmaterial, 25 °C, dieselbe Probe: Schritt | Volumen mL | n(Essigsäure) mmol | n(Acetat) mmol | pH
Start | 100 | 0,50 | 0,50 | 4,760
+0,30 mmol HCl (1 mL) | 101 | 0,80 | 0,20 | 4,158
+0,60 mmol NaOH (2 mL) | 103 | 0,20 | 0,80 | 5,362
+0,60 mmol HCl (2 mL) | 105 | 0,80 | 0,20 | 4,158
Verdünnungskontrolle: dieselbe Anfangszusammensetzung erhält nur Wasser auf 100/101/103/105 mL; beide Stoffmengen bleiben 0,50 mmol, pH jeweils 4,760. Kontrolle ohne Acetat: anfangs 100 mL Wasser mit einer Spur HCl auf pH 4,760; nach denselben Säure/Base-Zugaben modellierte pH-Werte 2,525 / 11,462 / 2,542, keine Acetat-Spezies. Auch diese Kontrolle kann also starke Indikatoränderungen zeigen. Alle Zahlen sind eigens erzeugte ideale Modellwerte, keine Messungen; Stoffanteile wurden nicht unabhängig vom Modell bestimmt. Im Lernauftrag sind keine pKa- oder pH-Rechnungen verlangt und keine Chemikalien zu handhaben.
materialEn:
Model material, 25 °C, the same sample: step | volume mL | n(acetic acid) mmol | n(acetate) mmol | pH
Start | 100 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 4.760
+0.30 mmol HCl (1 mL) | 101 | 0.80 | 0.20 | 4.158
+0.60 mmol NaOH (2 mL) | 103 | 0.20 | 0.80 | 5.362
+0.60 mmol HCl (2 mL) | 105 | 0.80 | 0.20 | 4.158
Dilution control: the same initial composition receives only water to 100/101/103/105 mL; both amounts remain 0.50 mmol and pH is 4.760 throughout. No-acetate control: initially 100 mL water adjusted to pH 4.760 with a trace of HCl; the same acid/base additions give modeled pH 2.525 / 11.462 / 2.542 with no acetate species. Thus this control can also produce strong indicator changes. All numbers are invented ideal model values, not measurements; species fractions were not determined independently of the model. The learner is asked neither to calculate pKa or pH nor to handle chemicals.
realExperimentalInferenceStillNeeded: Actual teacher-supervised acquisition with appropriate safety, known composition and calibrated pH/temperature/volume records.
Species-specific measurement calibrated independently of pH and of the Henderson-Hasselbalch relation, with validated selectivity and material recovery.
The same tracked sample must show the named species changing in both directions; blank and dilution controls must support the inference, with uncertainties and alternatives documented.
Model-generated fractions, synthetic spectra, a model answer or a returning indicator color do not meet these experimental evidence requirements.
